title: Yummy Creamy Japanese Tofu Kaiseki Course
description: A fatty and creamy Japanese dish from Okinawa, featuring enchilada sauce and katsuramuki-cut vegetables, served as a romantic kaiseki course.
instructions: Cut the tofu into small cubes and pan-fry until golden brown.
Prepare the katsuramuki-cut daikon, carrots, and lotus root by slicing them into thin strips.
In a large saucepan, combine the enchilada sauce, sesame oil, soy sauce, and mirin, and bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Add the pan-fried tofu and katsuramuki-cut vegetables to the saucepan and stir to coat with the sauce.
Reduce the heat to low and let the mixture simmer for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Serve the tofu and vegetables hot, garnished with sesame seeds and chopped scallions.
Prepare a small side of steamed rice and pickled ginger to accompany the dish.
Arrange the dish on a large platter or individual plates, in a visually appealing manner.
Refrigerate and consume within 1 week — this preparation is not shelf-stable without an approved acid level and canning process.

Refrigerator pickle only: store in the fridge and consume within 1 week. For shelf-stable canning, add at least 2 tablespoons of vinegar (5% acidity) per cup of brine and follow a tested water-bath process.
